If the pixel size did not change, nothing changes. Diagnostics record the DPI event and the (unchanged) `k`.
764	- **If `k_base` changes while at a ladder step** (a resize while `k_z ≠ k_base`): `k_base` is re-derived in the same `RESCALING` frame and the ladder `[1, k_base_new + 2]` rebuilt; `k_z` is kept if it is still on the ladder, else clamped to the nearer end; the step persists (it is never a hold); the field and the solver's `s` recompute. Example: 1920×1080 → 1280×720 while at `k_z = 2` keeps `k_z = 2`, which is now the default (`diag.zoom_step = 0`); the same resize while at `k_z = 5` clamps to 4 (`diag.zoom_step = +2`). Diagnostics record `diag.k_base`, `diag.k_z`, `diag.zoom_step = k_z − k_base`. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check.)*
765	
766	**Zoom**
767	
768	- **If the zoom input is pressed during a cut**: the cut completes first (the solver reset is one frame); the zoom step applies on the following frame as its own one-frame `RESCALING`. Two cuts in two frames are acceptable; a cut and a scale change in the same frame are not (two transforms to screenshot). Diagnostics record both with their frame numbers.
769	- **If `zoom_in` or `zoom_out` is pressed during `LOADING`**: the press is discarded (edge-triggered, never queued); the first `RUNNING` frame is the cut to the avatar at `k_base` after a re-wake, or at the pre-load `k_z` after an in-session load (zoom is pipeline state, never saved, reset only on re-wake); a press after that steps normally. The player never sees a zoomed re-wake frame. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check.)*
770	- **If `zoom_in` is pressed at `k_base + 2`, or `zoom_out` at `k_z = 1`**: ignored — no `RESCALING`, no cut; `diag.zoom_step_refused` increments. *(Added 2026-10-26 — consistency check.)*
771	- **If re-wake occurs while `k_z ≠ k_base`**: the re-wake `CUT` resets `k_z` to `k_base` so the cryo bay frames identically to the first wake; `diag.zoom_reset = REWAKE`. A body transfer, transit or in-session load leaves `k_z` unchanged across its cut. *(Added 2026-10-26 — consistency check.)*
772	- **If `zoom_out` is pressed down to 1× on a 2× world** (720p, Deck, manual 2×): `k_z = 1`, field = the full picture at 1 screen px per base px (Deck under `expand`: 1280×800 base = 26.7 × 16.7 tiles); 5.6 tier-2 marks are defined to survive 50 % so readability holds; the on-device acuity check is the accessibility-specialist's. **Draw-call consequence:** about 4× the default content is in view, so the Y-sorted layer's ≈ 300-draw ceiling (D.16) is tested at the zoomed Deck field, not at 1080p default — spike step 5 must include it (routed to technical-artist). **Lit pixels:** under pass B unchanged (the window is the window); under pass A — the default and the fallback — the world viewport renders at logical size, so the zoomed Deck target is 1280×800 texels = **4× the lit pixels of 640×400**, and light and shadow cost scales with it — the second reason steps 3 and 5 must be run at the largest ladder field of each target (1× on 1080p is 9× the default field). Diagnostics record `diag.k_z = 1`, the per-viewport draw count and the lit-pixel count. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check.)*
773	- **If a zoom step is pressed with reduced motion on**: the step still happens — it is a cut, not a motion, and it is the player's input. Look-ahead is already 0 under reduced motion, so the zoomed frame is centred on the avatar.
774	- **If a zoom step is pressed during a pause**: the press is discarded (the chart table owns input while paused and the world viewport is not re-rendering); the frozen frame stays at its current `k_z` (the world simply stopped, 7.4), and that `k_z` persists on resume with no `RESCALING`. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check.)*
775	
776	**Follow, cuts and target discontinuities**
777	
778	- **If the follow target teleports on re-wake**: `P_jump` fires (D.10) → cut; the solver resets to the target with `L = 0` (eased in at the slew rate, so the first frame does not depend on the aim at that instant) and jolt cleared *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; framing is identical to the first wake (same room, same lamp, same `pose_q` offset) — snap, not ease. Diagnostics record `diag.cut_reason = REWAKE` (the `LOADING → RUNNING` trigger) and the pose.
779	- **If the follow target teleports on pod arrival**: the arrival is a body transfer and a scene load → cut through `TRANSIT_HOLD`'s black; the first `PRESENTING` frame is already composed at the new body's frame. `diag.cut_reason = BODY_TRANSFER`.
780	- **If the avatar's body changes without a load** (weld merges the avatar's section into the ship; detach puts the avatar on a new body): the solver **rebases** (`BODY_TRANSFER`): `f` and its history shift by `frame_delta_px` into the new body frame and the lag and `L` are kept, so the avatar's screen position is unchanged and there is no cut *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; where the hull jump cannot be guaranteed zero it is a hard cut, never a pan. The detached section translates without rotation in the interior view. Body supplies `frame_delta_px` in `BODY_TRANSFER` and the pipeline decides (BDY-34); diagnostics record the old and new body IDs and `frame_delta_px`. Where Web Map & Transit cannot guarantee `docked(a, b, frame_shift_px)` before a PLAYER-origin weld, the pipeline hides every non-zero `delta_abs` with its C5 camera cut, so the player never sees the hull jump (BDY-27) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)*.
781	- **If a detach moves the camera's *limits* rather than its body** (the avatar stays on the ship, a section leaves): no cut; the `PROJECTOR` updates the limits rect the solver reads (`Camera2D.limit_*` stays at its defaults) on the next tick's notification *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; if the current pose is now outside the rect, the solver enters `CLAMPED` and the eased rect edge `rect_eff` carries the pose to the new edge along the D.6 exponential, 95 % in `t_95 = 0.54 s` with zero overshoot (D.8b: the pose is clamped against `rect_eff`, never popped) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Diagnostics record the limit change.
782	- **If the target exceeds the pan ceiling for exactly `T_PAN` minus one frame**: no cut; D.8 holds the avatar inside the inner box and D.6 eases. The predicate is "held continuously for ≥ `T_PAN`" in seconds — at 60 fps that is 6 frames (5 do not fire), at 144 fps 15 (14 do not), at 30 fps 3 (2 do not). Diagnostics record the peak `v_follow` and duration as `diag.pan_near_miss`.
783	- **If the lag is exactly `LAG_CUT` (48 px)**: no cut — the predicate is strictly greater. At 48.01 the solver cuts. Diagnostics record the lag sample. The invariant `LAG_CUT > v_max·τ_follow` (48 > 32.4) means a legal run never approaches it; if Player Controller raises `v_max` to 200 px/s or more at `τ = 0.18` and `L_MAX = 72`, Section G's inner-box check fails the build (the inner-box invariant binds before the 266 px/s lag-cut bound).
784	- **If `prev == curr` on the first frame after a restore**: `p = floor(prev)` for every `tick_alpha` — the correct outcome (nothing moved). The camera's `P_jump` sees the target jump from its pre-load position → cut (`LOADING → RUNNING` also forces it). Diagnostics record `diag.cut_reason = LOAD`.
785	- **If an owner forgot `previous := current` in `post_restore`**: the first frame after a load interpolates from the pre-load `previous` toward the restored `current` — a sprite drawn partway between two unrelated places for up to one tick, and the camera cuts anyway. This is a defect, not a tolerated state: a debug assertion in the pipeline root checks, on the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING`, that every moving read view reports `previous == current`, and diagnostics name the offending block (`diag.stale_previous = [block_id]`). Routed to the kernel (CR-8 `post_restore`) as a required step.
786	- **If the first `RUNNING` frame after any `LOADING` is not yet filtered for the restored sanity level**: it is not presented — the layer-1 black hold stays up across any rebuild (per-element Filter materials re-bound; the mask re-allocated if route (a) ships) until the frame is drawn through the Perception Filter for the restored sanity; no unfiltered frame is ever presented, because one clean frame would be a free oracle about a hallucination (Save/Load SL-24, H4; the Filter's `first_frame_filtered` counter) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format)*.
787	- **If the avatar and the aim stop** (a still scene): each pose term settles per axis once within `SETTLE_EPS` (D.6, D.7), so `pose_q` is constant after at most **`t_settle = max(t_settle_f, t_settle_L)`** (`t_settle_f` ≈ 0.75 s from the 32.4 px run lag; `t_settle_L` ≈ 2.5 s after a full 144 px aim reversal: 0.6 s at the slew clamp plus `τ_lookahead·ln(L_SLEW_MAX·τ_lookahead/SETTLE_EPS)` = 0.4 × ln(57.6/0.5) = 1.9 s; the final base pixel may land inside that window, as the last step of a motion the avatar or the player's aim caused) and equals `floor(target + L_target)`, approached from any of the four directions and with `L_MAX = 0`. Diagnostics record `diag.pose_settled_at` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
788	- **If `dt` is 0, negative or larger than `DT_MAX`, or `τ_follow_eff` is 0** (a hitch, a double-delivered frame, rigid follow): `dt ≤ 0` skips the solver update (no `0/0`, no NaN in the state); `dt` is clamped to `DT_MAX` = 0.05 s, the remaining real time arriving as a target discontinuity that D.10 treats (a hitch recovery is a named trigger of `P_jump` / `P_pan`); `τ_follow_eff ≤ τ_EPS` sets `a = 1` (rigid follow). Diagnostics record `diag.dt_clamped` and `diag.solver_skipped` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
789	- **If a zoom step is pressed while running at `v_max`**: the solver rescales `d = target − f` by `τ_follow_eff(new)/τ_follow_eff(old)` and `L` by `s_new/s_old` on the `RESCALING` frame (D.6), so the avatar's offset from picture centre in screen px is unchanged for `s ≤ 1`, the inner box does not engage and no cut fires *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
790	- **If `tick_alpha` is reported > 1 or < 0**: impossible by kernel D.3 (clamped at the driver); the pipeline asserts `0 ≤ tick_alpha ≤ 1` in debug and, in release, clamps and increments `diag.tick_alpha_out_of_range`. A non-zero counter is a kernel defect.
791	
792	**Jolt**
793	
794	- **If two jolt events arrive in one frame or overlap**: amplitude is the **max**, not the sum (`|j| ≤ JOLT_MAX = 2` always); the decay restarts from the later event. Diagnostics record both event IDs and the chosen `J_0`.
795	- **If a jolt event arrives with reduced motion on**: `J_0 = 0`; the event is logged (`diag.jolt_suppressed = true`) so audio and the HUD glyph still carry it. Also at MVP the knob default is 0 regardless.
796	- **If a jolt is active during a cut**: cleared by the reset (D.10). The cut frame has `j = 0`.
797	- **If a jolt is requested by anything other than a P1 physical event** (Attention, Sanity, horror presentation): refused at the API — the jolt entry point accepts only tagged physical events; a debug assertion fires and diagnostics record the caller (`diag.jolt_refused = [caller]`). This is C1's anchor enforced.
798

799	**Look-ahead**
800	
801	- **If the mouse is still while the lean swings, or while the avatar moves**: while the lean swings the aim is constant, because `mouse_to_world_aim` has no `L`, clamp or jolt in it (D.14b). A still cursor offset of 24, 48 or 72 base px from picture centre, a still avatar and `L` forced from 0 to 72 give the same committed `aim_angle` on every frame; a still cursor and an avatar at a **steady** run (follow lag settled) also give a constant aim, but while the lag is changing (run start, stop, a turn) the aim point moves with `f_q` by at most the lag change (≤ 32.4 px at the defaults, D.14b Example) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R4)*. Using `mouse_to_world_view` for aim would feed the lean back into the beam and is a lint failure. Diagnostics record `diag.aim_pose_read = [caller]` if aim code reads the view mapping *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
802	- **If the cursor crosses the avatar** (aim length below `LEAN_R0·s`): the lean magnitude `m` falls to 0 smoothly (D.7), so the frame returns to centre instead of swinging by `2·L_MAX`; the direction `û` holds its previous value inside `ε` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
803	- **If the player runs while aiming back at a pursuer** (aim opposite to the run, `m = 1`, `W_RUN` = 0.5): `L_target = (0, 0)`, so the frame is centred on the follow term (the avatar sits `lag_∞` = 32.4 px off-centre, inside the box) instead of leaning 72 px backward; aiming forward keeps the full 72 px lean; a diagonal aim gives the blended vector of D.7 (`|L| = 50.9` for a perpendicular aim). When the run stops or the avatar drops to a walk, `r` drops to 0 (the Controller's `loco_state` leaves `RUN`) and `L` eases to the pure-aim target at `τ_lookahead` under the slew clamp (the ease, not a ramp on `w`, is what prevents a pop); no cut predicate reads `L`. A run into a wall (no committed movement for 3 ticks, `moved` false) gives `w` = 0 the same way. A **diagonal** run or walk gives the same `w` and a constant `û_v` on every tick (the octant centre), where the displacement-keyed form jittered *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Reduced motion: `L_MAX = 0`, so no weighting *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
804	- **If the beam is off**: look-ahead follows the aim exactly as when it is on (reconciliation 3) — toggling the beam never moves the camera. Diagnostics record nothing special.
805	- **If the mouse aim flicks 180° in one frame**: `L_target` reverses; the slew clamp (D.7) limits the first frames to `144 × dt` px (2.4 px at 60 fps); 95 % of the reversal completes in ≈ 1.4 s; no cut predicate reads look-ahead, so no cut. The reversal is player-caused, satisfying C-R's 100 ms rule. Diagnostics record `diag.lookahead_slew_clamped = true` for the clamped frames.
806	- **If the aim is a zero vector or NaN** (no input yet, a disconnected device): `|aim| < ε` → `û` holds its previous value; on the very first frame of a session `û` defaults to the avatar's facing (down-screen south if none) and `L_target = L_MAX · û`. NaN is treated as zero. Diagnostics increment `diag.aim_invalid`.
807	- **If reduced motion is on**: `L_MAX = 0`, so `L_target = 0` and `L` eases to zero at the slew clamp when the setting is toggled mid-play; thereafter the camera is centred. Tremor, hairlines and audio carry the beam's forward information.
808	- **If look-ahead plus lag would push the avatar outside the inner box** (a 40 px target jump **south** while aiming north, opposite the lean: 40 + 72 = 112 > 108; a north jump gives 32 and does not engage the box) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: D.8 pins the pose at the box edge for the first frames; the avatar stays inside the central 60 %; no cut (the jump is below `JUMP_CUT`). Diagnostics record `diag.inner_box_engaged = true`.
809	
810	**Frame rate**
811	
812	- **If the render rate is 30 fps**: two ticks per frame; `tick_alpha` clamps at 1 after the second; a 1 px/tick body shows 2-px steps; input-to-pixel worst case 50 ms (kernel D.4); the solver's `T_PAN` is 3 frames; `present_time` advances 33 ms per frame. The sim is unchanged (`state_hash` identical across caps — the acceptance test).
813	- **If the render rate is 144 fps**: ticks on ≈ 42 % of frames; with interpolation and `Q = 1`, at `v_walk = 120` 16.7 % of frames repeat the pose (D.17) *(re-run 2026-10-26 — consistency check)* — honest, not a bug; never a backward or doubled step (step 12). `T_PAN` is 15 frames. If testers name the stutter, the `Q = 1/k` path removes it above 48 px/s.
814	- **If the panel is 40 Hz or 90 Hz** (Steam Deck options): rates not multiples of 60; the interpolation path keeps steps whole-base-pixel (alternating 1 and 2 base px for a 1 px/tick body at 40 fps) — at 40 fps `tick_alpha` alternates ≈ 0.5 / 1.0, at 90 fps ≈ 0.33 / 0.67 / 1.0. Spiked at both caps (step 13). Diagnostics record `Engine.get_frames_per_second()` and the repeated-pose count.
815	- **If the render rate falls below 20 fps**: the kernel runs up to `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks then lets sim time lag (CR-17); a catch-up burst is at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` × 3 px = 12 px, below `JUMP_CUT`, so it eases under D.6/D.8 and never cuts; a ≥ 48 px displacement in one frame needs a named source (a weld delta, a Body shove, a restore) and cuts (`P_jump`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The pipeline never compensates visually. Diagnostics record frame time, ticks per frame and the kernel's lag counter.
816	
817	**Sorting and drawing**
818	
819	- **If two Y-sorted items have the same sort origin** (two actors on one row; an actor on the first legal row south of a wall): the key is `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` (PR-5, D.12), so an actor sorts after a wall, prop, door or machinery node of equal `sort_y` and draws over its face at every `x`, and two actors on one row order by `actor_id`. The order is deterministic across runs and across a save and reload, and independent of `x`: an actor walking past a prop's `x` on an equal row never changes the draw order (→ the tie-break ADR for the mechanism, `[UNV]`). Diagnostics do not record ties (they are normal) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
820	- **If an actor stands exactly on a wall footprint line** (`y_foot = y_0 + 24`, the footprint's south edge): this row is the first legal row south of the wall (the footprint rows are collision); `sort_y` equal → tie → class rank → actor over face. If physics ever places a foot box overlapping a SOLID rect (`solid_in`) the actor is behind the wall by D.12 and visibly wrong — a Ship Body collision defect, caught by the debug tree-walk's "actor inside footprint" check; a foot box inside a passable door's gap is **not** that defect and never fires it. Diagnostics record `diag.actor_in_footprint` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
821	- **If an actor walks through a door or doorway** (`area > 0`): the door sorts by its footprint's north edge (PR-5, D.12), so the actor is behind the frame while `y_foot < y_0`, over it while `y_0 ≤ y_foot`, and its head is visible throughout the crossing from either side; the door cannot close on the actor (Layout LY-11), so the sort switch to `y_0 + 24` never happens with an actor inside. A door that is closed (`area = 0`) is a wall. Diagnostics record nothing (a normal case) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
822	- **If a prop is taller than the 72 px face** (`f > 72`, e.g. a 96-px-tall machinery node placed flush against a wall): its top rows overlap the cap band (D.12 cap rows), and because caps draw above the Y-sort band the cap is drawn over the prop's top — visibly wrong. Outcome: the kit rule "face height ≤ 72 for anything flush against a wall" is enforced by the asset checklist (8.9 addition, routed to art-director/level-designer); at runtime the debug tree-walk flags any Y-sorted item whose top row is above `sort_y − 72` while within 24 px of a wall footprint (`diag.cap_overlap = [item]`). Machinery nodes' own caps (96×96 cells) are part of the node sprite, not the cap layer, so a node *not* against a wall is fine.
823	- **If a horror segment is rotated under nearest sampling**: pass A — stair-stepped on the base grid, accepted; pass B — angled k×k blocks, tolerated for horrors and web only (8.4); the rotation is quantised to 15° (a test) and stepped at 12 fps. If the step-2 review rejects the pass-B look, 8.10's remedies apply (24-angle sets or a base-resolution sub-viewport for horrors → ADR). A human-built node with `rotation ≠ 0` is a lint failure, not a tolerated state (`diag.rotated_human_geometry = [node]`).
824	- **If the z-band window would overflow** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the bands are world-anchored, so the count depends on the height of the union rect of the bodies drawn (loaded plus docked / detaching), not the field (D.13) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `N_bands_body` ≤ 889 at `BAND_H = 24` (a body up to 21 336 rows); a taller body, or a `BAND_H` small enough to exceed the window (`BAND_H` 1 on a 2 880-row body), **refuses the fallback** — the Y-sort node stays whole, `diag.zband_overflow` records the body and the count, and nothing is clamped (a clamped band would mis-order walls against actors). Section G flags `BAND_H < 12` as unsafe for this reason.
825	- **If the Y-sorted layer exceeds ≈ 300 draws at the spike**: the D.13 fallback is built behind a flag and its **go/no-go runs**: draw calls and CPU with it on must both be lower than with it off at the largest ladder field of each target; if so it is enabled (wall faces and the wall-mounted layer leave the Y-sort node, nothing visible changes), otherwise it is withdrawn and the lever is the per-field draw cap (D.16). Diagnostics record per-viewport draw counts and CPU before and after *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
826	
827	**Filter, layers and the HUD**
828	
829	- **If the Perception Filter pass runs with no truth-channel mask available** (route (a) built but its mask viewport failed to allocate): the pass **is not applied** — the pipeline root sets the container's material to null and the world is shown unfiltered rather than letting trails, sprites, beams or the true cone edge be touched (Pillar 1: a lie that corrupts the truth channel is the one failure the game cannot have). Per-element Filter materials inside layer 0 still run. Diagnostics record `diag.filter_pass_disabled = NO_MASK`; the Debug Overlay shows it in red. **At MVP (route PER_ELEMENT) the container material is null by design**: `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT`, container state `NOT_USED`, not shown red; `NO_MASK` (red) applies only when route (a) is built and its mask fails to allocate (registry `filter_route`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from perception-filter)*.
830	- **If a HUD element is accidentally parented into the world `SubViewport`**: it is lit, glowed, filtered and scrolls with the camera — immediately visible; the debug tree-walk lints "any `Control` or node in the `hud` group under the world viewport" and fails the dev build (`diag.hud_in_world = [node]`). Release builds have no automatic remedy; the lint is in CI.
831	- **If a stray script sets `Camera2D.zoom` to anything but `(1,1)`**: the debug tree-walk (every frame behind the console toggle, and always at startup) resets it to `(1,1)`, logs the writer's stack and increments `diag.camera_zoom_violation`; the one frame rendered at the wrong zoom is accepted in dev and impossible in release because the startup assertion fails the build if any script references `Camera2D.zoom` as a writer (lint). Zoom-out is a logical-size change, never this property.
832	- **If `physics_interpolation` is turned on by a setting or a scene**: the startup assertion fails (`physics/common/physics_interpolation == false` is asserted); if toggled at runtime, the tree-walk logs `diag.second_interpolator = PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION` and the pipeline root sets `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF` on every presentation node it owns. The symptom it prevents: a sprite swimming 1–3 render px against the camera at 144 fps while looking fine at 60.
833	- **If the letterbox bars are touched by a post-process** (a Filter pass or a `BackBufferCopy` sized to the window instead of the picture): the bars are outside the world viewport and the container, so a correctly placed pass cannot reach them; if a pass is found to cover the window, it is a defect — the startup assertion checks the container's rect equals the picture rect, and the debug tree-walk flags any `CanvasItem` on the root whose rect exceeds the picture (`diag.bar_overdraw = [node]`). Bars stay true black; the optional Graphite hairline is a HUD element inside the picture edge, never in the bar.
834	- **If the HR-15 ambient-floor step is raised to its maximum**: hull geometry only brightens by the measured floor + `HR15_STEP_MAX` (3) steps (Lighting's material) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)*; web, horrors and filaments stay beam-only; the HUD is untouched; the pipeline changes nothing — recorded here because it is the one brightness control the player has and a tester will look for a gamma slider that does not exist (`diag` records the HR-15 step in the frame header).
835	
836	**Flash clamp and photosensitivity**
837	
838	- **If a light's flash count would exceed `F_MAX = 3` in any 1 s window**: Lighting's modifier contract holds the light at its last compliant luminance until the window admits the next transition (the clamp *delays* transitions, it never brightens or darkens beyond the requested levels); the pipeline's flash scan records `(light_id, F, window_start_tick, clamped_transitions)`. The alarm beacon and the cryo gutter never trigger it; an unspecified deployable flicker might — hence the routed number.
839	- **If two individually compliant lights overlap one region (a ninth of the displayed picture at the current field) and their sum exceeds the regional ceiling**: the regional check catches it; the newer light's transitions are delayed first (it is the one that pushed the region over). Diagnostics record `(region_index, F_region, light_ids)`. The frame-mean check is evaluated after the regional one and catches the case where many regions are each just under.
840	- **If "reduce flashing" and "reduced motion" are both on**: both apply — deployables steady, arcs held as glow, beacon static mark + sound + HUD glyph, cryo gutter kept (flashing); look-ahead 0, jolt 0, world effects per HR-8 (motion). Neither touches trail propagation or `present_time`. No conflict: one is luminance, the other is motion.
841	- **If a full-frame flash is requested by any layer** (a hypothetical "white-out" effect): refused by construction — no API exists to write the whole frame's luminance; a shader that attempts it on the container violates PR-10 ("only adds violet/flesh at 4.4's places") and the flash scan's frame-mean check records it as a defect (`diag.frame_mean_flash`).
842	
843	**Startup and configuration**
844	
845	- **If `project.godot` is missing a required key** (the `[display]` block, `default_texture_filter`, either `snap_2d_*` key, `hdr_2d`, `use_debanding`, the default clear colour, the two window size overrides, the HDR-output flag) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the debug startup assertion fails loudly with the key name, and the headless gdUnit4 parse test fails in CI before any window exists. Diagnostics (if the dev build is run anyway) print the full read-back table: `content_scale_mode`, `content_scale_stretch`, `content_scale_size`, world viewport filter/snap/hdr/debanding members, container `texture_filter`, `physics_interpolation`, `position_smoothing_enabled`, `Camera2D.zoom`, driver name.
846	- **If the world `SubViewport` does not read back the project's filter/snap settings** (propagation is NOT SOURCEABLE): the pipeline root sets the viewport's own members explicitly at boot regardless, so the read-back passes either way; step 11 records whether the explicit set was necessary.
847	- **If the driver reported at startup is not the one the spike measured** (`vulkan` `[BIN]` default vs D3D12 `[REF]`): nothing in this GDD assumes a driver; the name is logged (`diag.driver`) and V-sync/swap-chain behaviour is re-measured once on the other driver (step 13).
848	
849	- **If the window is wider than 16:9 and `expand` is enabled**: the visible base field widens up to the 960×540 cap at the same integer `k`; the extra columns show whatever is there — honest void in every dark state, and extra lit floor only where loops are running (chiefly the stable home-ship). No information the beam has not paid for is revealed, because unlit geometry remains at the ambient floor and web content is never drawn unlit. Diagnostics record the expanded base size. *(Creative-director recommendation, ratified by the user 2026-10-26 — Open Question 9.)*

943	## Visual/Audio Requirements
944	
945	The pipeline draws nothing of its own and plays nothing. What it *requires* of visual systems is the contract in Section C: every presentation element lives in the world `SubViewport` or on the root HUD layer, never both; every sprite and tile is placed at integer base pixels by presentation code (the viewport snap flags are a safety net, not the mechanism); human-built geometry never rotates at runtime; horror rigs and web pieces rotate only in the quantised steps the art bible fixes; VFX and one-off sprites use even cell sizes or `centered = false` with an integer offset so no origin lands on a half pixel; hairlines are sprites, never 1-px line draws (4.7 draws lines without an antialiasing feather). Two art-bible rules become pipeline rules here: the only brightness control in the game is the bounded ambient-floor step implemented as the hull-material raise (HR-15; no full-frame gamma or brightness exists), and letterbox bars, where they occur, are true black outside the world and get a 1-HUD-px Graphite hairline at the viewport edge so a bar is never read as unlit hull (routed to art-director); the hairline is a layer-1 element, excluded from the HUD's critical-strip count *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)*. Audio: none, except that the pipeline's render-rate loop is not the sim clock and audio cues keyed to tells must come from the simulation's notifications, never from frame events. No asset-spec flag: there are no assets.

946	
947	## Game Feel
948	
949	The camera is the one piece of this system the player feels, and its feel target is **absence**: a window bolted to the ship, not a lens that performs.
950	
951	- **Stillness.** When the crewmate stops, the frame stops — within the follow time constant and then exactly: the per-axis settle (`SETTLE_EPS`, D.6/D.7) is the mechanism that makes "exactly" true, and the last base pixel can land up to ≈ 0.75 s after the stop (the follow term `f`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the look-ahead `L` keeps easing for up to ≈ 2.5 s after a full aim reversal, which is **player-caused** (the aim moved it) and is not the avatar's stop, so "the frame stops" is measured on `f` for a stop and on `L` only after the aim has stopped too; the settle is `max(t_settle_f, t_settle_L)` per axis *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. No bounce, no overshoot (the first-order follow cannot overshoot by construction), no idle drift, no breathing. The frame is the still thing readings move inside (art bible 7.3).
952	- **Follow.** First-order exponential follow, τ ≈ 0.18 s, no dead-zone by default (a dead-zone starts and stops discontinuously, which reads as "something happened"); the crewmate is held inside the central ~60 % of the frame at walking and running speed. Lag at run speed ≈ 0.6 tile.
953	- **Look-ahead.** The frame leans where the beam points: 1.5 tiles (72 px) along the aim direction by default, range 1.0–1.56 tiles (48–75 px), eased over τ ≈ 0.40 s from the *local raw* aim so a mouse flick does not yank the frame, with the mouse aim measured open-loop (the lean never turns the beam) and the lean scaled by aim magnitude *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; while running, half the lean follows the direction of movement (`LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT` 0.5), so a runner aiming straight back sees a centred frame rather than a backward one *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. This buys back cone rim on the short axis exactly when the player is looking there — because they looked, not because the game did.
954	- **Motion quantum.** The camera moves in whole base pixels (MVP). Motion at walking speed is uniform stepping, which reads as smooth; the 1/k-screen-pixel quantum is the named upgrade if testers name the stutter, and needs art-director and ux-designer sign-off because it lets the hero sprite wobble ±0.5 base px against the frame.
955	- **Rhythm independence.** Identical camera constants in boarding and breach; the frantic feeling comes from more things moving in the world, never from the frame fighting the player (art bible 2.8). Identical input traces produce identical camera traces in calm, tell and breach — an acceptance criterion, not a hope.
956	- **Cuts, not pans.** Re-wake, pod arrival, a body transfer whose hull jump is not guaranteed zero and any follow failure (pan-speed ceiling exceeded, lag over one tile — `LAG_CUT` 48 px, a 48-px jump) are cuts; a weld or detach transfer is a rebase that moves nothing on screen *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The camera never pans across geography the player did not walk.
957	- **No shake in MVP.** A bounded physical jolt (≤ 2 base px, decayed, on hull separation / docking / detach only, never on Attention or sanity) exists as a knob defaulting to 0, to be revisited at VS-A once the HUD-still-over-moving-world read is tested. Hull stress goes into real needles, dust and hairlines.
958	- **Latency.** Input-to-pixel is the kernel's ≤ 1 tick plus one render frame; acknowledgement is same-frame on the presentation side. At 30 fps motion shows every second tick's pose honestly; at 144 and 90 fps interpolation with `tick_alpha` places each base-pixel step at the right instant and never twice in a frame; at 40 fps steps alternate 1 and 2 base px *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)*.
959	- **Accessibility couplings.** Reduced motion disables look-ahead, zeroes the jolt and applies the HR-8 world-effect reductions listed in PR-14 and Tuning Knobs (static direction shapes, static alarm mark); it never suppresses trails, tremor, hairlines or audio. "Reduce flashing" is a separate toggle. Neither alters the tick.
960	
961	*Anti-targets*: cinematic takeover, revealing pans, auto-aim, free-look, sanity wobble, handheld energy, Dutch tilt, non-integer or tweened zoom, sub-pixel camera position.

964	
965	No player-facing UI of its own, but the pipeline defines three surfaces other systems' UI must fit:
966	
967	1. **The HUD layer contract** (consumed by HUD & Suit Layer, Chart Table, Crew Strip, Interaction prompts): a root-viewport `CanvasLayer` outside the world `SubViewport`, integer-scaled at `H_default = max(k, 3)` — never below 3× on any display, player-raisable to 2×H in integer steps, labelled by resulting cap height; authored anchor-relative to the visible viewport edges with a 5 % safe margin in HUD pixels, surviving a fractional logical canvas (Steam Deck 1280×800 ÷ 3) and both `keep` and `expand` aspects; exempt by construction from world glow, ambient, occlusion, the Perception Filter pass, camera motion and jolt (HR-1, HR-13). World-anchored prompts project through the *unjolted* camera transform and are drawn only for lit objects; they never clamp to the frame edge. *Consequence routed to art-director*: on the Deck the 3× HUD over a 2× world exceeds 7.0's 12 % × 5 % critical-strip cap by default.
968	2. **The Settings surface** (consumed by Settings & Input Rebinding and Accessibility Settings — Alpha systems, but the hooks exist from MVP): display mode (fullscreen / borderless / windowed), resolution, world scale (Auto = largest integer that fits, plus an explicit integer list; manual scale below Auto forces `keep`), HUD scale, reading-face scale, aspect `keep` / `expand` once `expand` ships post-spike, frame cap and VSync (`ENABLED` default; `MAILBOX` as uncapped-no-tear; never `ADAPTIVE` by default), look-ahead strength (off / short / default; added to PR-14 by the amendment note below), reduce flashing (**default ON at first launch** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; jolt strength is hidden until the VS-A jolt decision — a setting for a feature that ships at 0 is not exposed), reduced motion, and the bounded HR-15 ambient-floor step. So the "constant lag" claim only holds when the target lands on integer positions, which happens at 60fps but not at 144fps where fractional alignment causes the offset to alternate — meaning the AC's universality claim breaks down depending on framerate.

285:**Crewmate identity is carried by beam shape, not sprite hue.** Pillar 1's human channel says a crewmate's own beam — colour *and shape* — is never faked, which makes the beam the identity object. Up to four players, so **four directional beam shapes**: wide cone, narrow cone, split (twin) beam, and broad fan (short and wide). All four stay inside the Tungsten family (Section 4) with at most a small temperature offset; the differentiator is shape because shape survives colorblindness and four beam hues would eat palette the loops need. Half-angle, reach and edge width per shape are tabulated in 8.3 (provisional until 8.12 step 2). *(Amended per AD-ART-BIBLE review 2026-10-25)* The beam originates at a chest-mounted lamp (a per-facing chest point, 5.6), hands-free: the hands and the tool layer carry no light. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — user decision: chest-mounted lamp)* Helmet trim carries a matching stripe count (1–4) for the still frame. *Alternative considered*: per-player suit colour, the co-op default. Rejected — it spends four hues in a game that must keep hue scarce, and a suit colour is a sprite property a hallucination could plausibly be imagined to fake, whereas the beam is a light the engine renders honestly.
413:Depth never changes hue. It changes two things. The table is an **ordering contract** — outer > middle > inner — whose values are spike-written per 8.12 step 7 (8.11 flag 1); the percentages are targets, not settings. *(Amended per 8.11 flag 1)*
456:**Docked-pod status glow vs the visible-unknown lamp** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)***.** Ruling X2 (design-review decisions, Web Map option B) gives every dock room a small self-powered status glow on the docked-podcraft prop; it counts as an ordinary lit fixture for the console's lit gate (6.3 rule 9). It must never read as the wreck's one visible unknown (2.5), so it is separated from the lamp on luminance, not hue. *Constraint:* the glow's source sprite sits at least one usable ladder gap below the **lowest** lamp the unknown may use. *Derivation:* the unknown is "Tungsten or a loop hue" (2.5, 6.3 rule 4), so its source sprite may be Coolant Ice (≈ 91), Tungsten fixture `#FFCC66` (≈ 85), Power Amber (≈ 81), O₂ Cyan (≈ 79) or Fuel Ember (≈ 61); the smallest documented usable gap on this ladder is 12 L* (Tungsten beam vs Power Amber, above). No value lies at least 12 from both Fuel Ember (61) and O₂ Cyan (79) between them (it would have to be at least 73 and at most 67), so the glow goes below the lowest option: ceiling = 61 − 12 = 49 L*. *Value:* the glow's source sprite is Tungsten-hue (≈ 40°, so no new hue and no loop colour) at reduced value, `#886C35` (L* ≈ 47; margin to Fuel Ember 61 − 47 = 14 ≥ 12; to the Tungsten fixture 85 − 47 = 38). *Worked check:* hue of `#886C35` = 60° × (108 − 53) / (136 − 53) ≈ 40°. *Known collision, accepted:* L* ≈ 47 shares a rung with Alarm Red and the Violet core; hue keeps it Tungsten-family and it never sweeps, pulses or edges, so neither reserved colour is borrowed. The hex is **provisional** `[PLACEHOLDER — confirm in the lighting spike, 8.12, and a dark-dock still]`; the 12 L* constraint and the 49 ceiling are the rule, the hex is the current candidate. The glow's emitted energy and radius are the Emitter's and Lighting's numbers (EM-3/EM-11 amendment), not this section's; the art requirement on them is only that the glow reads as the dimmest light in a lit dock room.
891:- **Low-vision ambient floor (HR-15, user decision 6).** A per-client option raising the scene's ambient floor to **the measured ring floor plus a bounded number of steps** (provisional: floor + 2–3 steps of the 8-bit frame, set from 8.12 step 7; always below the 10 % stable state of 2.3 so "powered" still reads as the warmest state — this replaces the earlier absolute "≤ 6 %", which 8.11 flag 1 showed is not a meaningful unit before the floor is measured *(Amended per AD-ART-BIBLE review 2026-10-25)*), revealing **hull geometry only** — the web, horrors and filaments remain visible only in direct light, exactly as before — and touching **no simulation**: Attention is unchanged, because the raised ambient is not a light the crew is running. This is a bounded exception to Principle 1's "rooms are unlit", decided for accessibility and recorded with its costs in 7.6. The technical-artist owns the rendering (raised ambient on hull albedo that does not count as illumination for web-grammar content).
992:15. **HR-15 Ambient-floor option is bounded.** The low-vision ambient option raises the floor to the measured ring floor + 2–3 steps (provisional, per 7.4 and 8.12 step 7; below the 10 % stable state *(Amended per AD-ART-BIBLE review 2026-10-25)*), reveals hull geometry only (web, horrors and filaments still only in direct light), does not touch the Attention simulation, and is per-client. *Adopted per decision 6; costs recorded in 7.6 item 16; rendering → technical-artist.*
1081:**The four beam shapes and the other lights — numbers (provisional — confirmed in 8.12 step 2).** Referenced from 3.2. Values are chosen so the four player shapes light roughly equal areas (∝ half-angle × reach²), so no shape dominates; the game-designer tunes from here. All four beam shapes originate at the per-facing chest point (`anchor_chest_<facing>`, 5.6), not at the hand; reach is measured from that point. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — user decision: chest-mounted lamp)* Edge width is the hard outer edge of hero #1 (3.5): under pass A it is one base pixel by construction; under pass B it is a 1–2 px edge in the light texture, scaled. The narrow cone and the beacon at 8 tiles exceed what a 2048² light texture covers at 6× (≈ 7.1 tiles); under pass B at 2160p either the texture ceiling rises for those two or their rim softens slightly — accepted either way. *(Amended per AD-ART-BIBLE review 2026-10-25)*
1090:| Glowstick pool (thrown) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — user decision: glowsticks)* | 360° | radius 2 / 96 at full life, waning with it (radius number provisional — game-designer; spike-confirmed in 8.12 step 2) | soft — no hard edge; **steady, never flickers**, then waning (3.2); Chemlight `#86B896` (4.1) | omnidirectional; thrown on a short arc, lands as a world light | none by default (non-shadow); counts toward the same sixth-slot and lighting-budget rules as the deployable pool (8.11 flag 2) |
1102:Option names, types and defaults below carry the technical-artist's sourcing legend: `[BIN]` = read from the installed 4.7.2 editor's class dump (existence, types, defaults and enum values only — never behaviour or cost); `[REF]` = the pinned `docs/engine-reference/godot/` (which covers neither 2D texture import nor 2D lighting; the `[BIN]` facts here are worth folding into it); `[UNV-4.3]` = training-era knowledge, used only where a spike test is named alongside it; `NOT SOURCEABLE` = measured by the spike (8.12), never guessed. Note for anyone arriving from Godot 3: texture *filtering* is no longer an import flag — it is a `CanvasItem` property with a project default — so "filter off" is set once at project level and overridden only on the `light_` category.
1106:**Texture import preset (project Import Defaults for `texture`, then per-folder overrides) — adopted from the technical-artist.** Defaults are `[BIN]`; the *meaning* of each integer (that `compress/mode 0` is Lossless, that `detect_3d/compress_to 0` is Disabled) is `[UNV-4.3]` and is confirmed in the Import dock during the spike (8.12, step 6).
1121:**Render mode (an art call with a technical price — recorded as IDEAL plus fallback; the spike's pass A/B settles it).** The IDEAL is **sprites on the grid, light off the grid**: every sprite integer-scaled with nearest sampling while lights, occluder shadows and glow render at window resolution. The beam is engine light, not a drawing (6.2's logic applied to hero #1), and its soft interior falloff should be smooth; rendering it at base resolution steps it into 3 px bands at 1080p and makes the light "look drawn", folding hero #1 into the sprite layer. The technical-artist's architecture makes both passes one scene: the root viewport, with the stretch settings above, carries only the HUD `CanvasLayer` and a `SubViewportContainer` (`stretch = true` `[BIN]`); the world sits in a `SubViewport` with `use_hdr_2d`, `use_debanding`, `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `canvas_item_default_texture_filter = NEAREST` `[BIN]`. **Pass A**: the `SubViewport` at 640×360, scaled by the container — lights at base resolution, every cone edge, shadow edge and rotated segment on the pixel grid, one ninth of the lit pixels. **Pass B**: the `SubViewport` at window size with `size_2d_override = 640×360` and `size_2d_override_stretch = true` `[BIN]` — logical base coordinates, sprites integer-scaled, lights and shadows at window resolution. Whether `Light2D` resolves at the viewport's render size and whether `size_2d_override` behaves this way are both `[UNV-4.3]`; 8.12 step 2 is the test, and the cost difference is the 9× lever of 8.11 flag 4. **The fallback the art-director accepts is pass A**: a 3-px stair-step on the cone edge keeps 3.5's "hard outer edge" and loses only the smoothness of the interior falloff, which debanding partly recovers. Consequence under pass B: horror rig segments rotating under nearest sampling produce 3×3 blocks at an angle — the same pixel density, off the grid. **This is tolerated for horrors and web only** (3.3: the web never aligns to the grid) and **forbidden for anything human-built**, which is never rotated at runtime; if the off-grid look fails review, the technical-artist's remedies are pre-rotated segment sets (24 angles, a tool step) or a base-resolution sub-viewport for horrors alone. Sub-pixel blur is forbidden everywhere; 5.4's quantised rotation (15°) and stepped playback (12 fps) stand.

content.content:
**D.3 Render interpolation**

The `tick_alpha` formula is defined as:

`tick_alpha = clamp(t_since_last_commit / tick_duration, 0, 1)`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| t_since_last_commit | float | 0–unbounded wall-seconds | calculated (by the tick *driver*, not the sim) | Wall time since the last P4 commit; equivalently `acc / TICK_UNITS × tick_duration` from the driver's accumulator after the frame's steps (D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| tick_duration | float | 0.0167 s | calculated | D.1 |
| tick_alpha | float | 0.0–1.0 | calculated | Fraction of the way from the previous committed state to the current one |

**Output Range:** 0 at the instant of commit, 1 when a full tick has elapsed; clamped at 1 so that during a hitch or catch-up lag presentation holds the latest committed pose rather than extrapolating past it (extrapolation would show the ship doing something the sim has not yet done — a Pillar 1 hazard). The sim never reads this value (H9); only the driver computes it and only `PRESENTATION`/`PROJECTOR` consume it. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; disagreement resolved per the creative-director: the systems-designer fix.)* **While the kernel is not `RUNNING` the driver holds `tick_alpha` at 1.0** (presentation draws the latest committed pose, never the previous one), and **on every transition into `RUNNING` the kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every `interpolated` block**, so `previous == current` on resume and the first running frame — including a 0-tick frame (the transition frame runs none, CR-1a) — cannot interpolate backwards or across a discontinuity; a pause therefore never snaps a sprite back to its previous tick. At the shipped `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0` the clamp branch is unreachable in a `RUNNING` frame (after forgiveness `acc < TICK_UNITS`, so the unclamped value is < 1); the clamp is retained for the non-`RUNNING` hold and the fixture `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS > 0`.
**Example:** 7 ms after commit at 60 Hz → `7/16.67 = 0.42`; a position read view exposes `prev + (curr − prev) × 0.42`.

**D.4 Input-to-effect latency**

The `apply_tick` formula is defined as:

`apply_tick(c) = queued_tick_c + 1 + floor(q_pos_c / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK)`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|

Looking at the 30 fps example, I think the documentation's claim that "tick_alpha clamps at 1" is actually wrong — with exact integer accumulator arithmetic, alpha should alternate between 0 and 0.5, not 0.5 and 1.0, since the kernel uses integer TICK_UNITS for precision. This seems like a wording fix rather than an actual oracle violation, but I'm now noticing a deeper issue: at 144 fps with 1px/tick commits, floor(prev + α) equals prev for any α less than 1, meaning the interpolated position only changes exactly when a new tick commits — not smoothly across frames as intended.

For a 3px/tick runner, though, this changes things — per-frame deltas become 1-2px rather than a clean single step, which still satisfies "never twice per frame" for 1px/tick bodies but raises questions about whether that guarantee extends to faster-moving bodies at various frame rates like 60 vs 144 fps.

But for run speed at 180 px/s, 144 fps gives 1.25 px per frame, meaning the step can jump to 2 pixels — and at 90 fps it's exactly 2 px every frame. findings.section: Acceptance Criteria > Camera follow, look-ahead, cuts (mouse-aim AC, L1059) vs D.14b Example/Output Range (L644-645), Edge Cases L801, OQ 18
findings.finding: This is the same defect class as the three prior blockers: an (auto) AC whose oracle a correct implementation fails (G4). L1059 says that with a still cursor and a running avatar the aim is 'constant once the follow lag has settled' and shifted 'by exactly f_q - p, 32 px west of it ... 32 = floor(32.4)'. D.6 says lag is measured after the update. That lag is 30.9 px at 60 fps, 31.4 at 90 and 31.8 at 144, not lag_inf = 32.4. So f_q - p is 31 at 60 fps and 31 or 32 at 144 fps depending on the fractional part of the interpolated target. The D.14b Example repeats the error: 'floor(1000 - 32.4) = 967' is a shift of 33, and it then says 'moved 33 px'. The 'constant' claim is also false at 90 and 144 fps. f_q = floor(f) is taken from the interpolated target and changes every frame, while the Controller subtracts AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos_curr) + (0, -35), which steps once per tick (3 px at run). The aim can therefore differ by up to one tick's displacement, plus the independent-floor effect, even with a settled lag. There is no fixture dt in the AC.
findings.fix: Recompute from D.6/D.14b (G4). Rewrite the oracle as: 'with the cursor still and the avatar at a steady run, aim_point_shift = f_q - floor(pos_curr) is within 1 base px of -(lag_ss(dt) + tick_phase) and varies by no more than ceil(v/60) + 1 base px at 90 and 144 fps; exactly constant only at 60 fps with integer targets.' Give the dt explicitly and use lag_ss(dt) (30.9 at 60 fps, 31.8 at 144), as L1069 already does. In D.14b and Edge Cases L801, state the sawtooth bound, and state that the 32.4 px figure is the dt -> 0 upper bound, not the value that is drawn. Mirror the bound in Player Controller AC-PCI-056 and its Edge Case L797.

findings.section: Formulas D.14b Output Range (L644) / D.8b (L503) / C4 (L163) / OQ 18 - CLAMPED aim mismatch
findings.finding: Carried over; the previous pass did not land it. The GDD bounds the aim-vs-picture mismatch (pose_q - f_q) by L plus the inner-box correction, 'up to L_MAX_eff = 72' or '104 px' in C4 and OQ 18. D.8b states the limits clamp acts on the pose and 'the aim mapping's f_q is unaffected'. While the camera is CLAMPED, the picture centre c can sit far from f_q. D.8b's own example puts the avatar 170 px below picture centre while f_q = 960 and c = 820. A mouse player who places the cursor on a visible target near the hull edge gets cursor_world_aim = f_q + cursor_off, which is 140 px or more from the target. The beam then points away from, or even opposite to, where the cursor sits. That breaks the chest lamp, the game's main verb, whenever the camera is clamped. No AC covers it, and OQ 18's playtest item names only the lag + L case. The R4 ruling (f_q is canonical) is not reversed, but this consequence is not stated or bounded.
findings.fix: Keep R4's published f_q but make it limits-consistent. Publish f_q' = clamp(f_q, lo, hi), the same limits clamp applied to the follow term only, with no L, no inner-box and no jolt. That keeps the aim loop open, because the rect comes from the PROJECTOR, and it cuts the worst-case mismatch to at most L_MAX_eff. Update the D.14b Output Range and the registry mouse_to_world_aim entry. Add an AC: 'camera CLAMPED at hi_y, cursor on the avatar's sprite, aim direction points at the avatar to within AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX'. Player Controller conforms to the published value.

findings.section: Formulas D.6b (L445) vs D.8b (L503) vs D.9, registry follow_offset_quantised / limits_clamp

D.6b says pose_q = p + floor(o/Q)*Q 'the limits clamp (D.8b) is then applied to pose_q', and the registry follow_offset_quantised agrees ('then limits_clamp'). D.8b and the registry limits_clamp say the limits clamp comes first and 'then quantisation (D.9)' ('pose before quantisation'). D.6b is the default candidate. On that path an integer pose_q is clamped against lo/hi computed from the eased float rect_eff. For the transient after a detach or weld that moves the rect, the final pose is then non-integer, which breaks the whole-base-px camera rule and Pillar 1. No AC catches it: L1094 checks canvas scale only, and L1041 checks CanvasItem positions, not the canvas transform.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria > Camera follow, look-ahead, cuts (mouse-aim AC, L1059) vs D.14b Example/Output Range (L644-645), Edge Cases L801, OQ 18
findings.finding: This is the same defect class as the three prior blockers: an (auto) AC whose oracle a correct implementation fails (G4). L1059 says that with a still cursor and a running avatar the aim is 'constant once the follow lag has settled' and shifted 'by exactly f_q - p, 32 px west of it ... 32 = floor(32.4)'. D.6 says lag is measured after the update. That lag is 30.9 px at 60 fps, 31.4 at 90 and 31.8 at 144, not lag_inf = 32.4. So f_q - p is 31 at 60 fps and 31 or 32 at 144 fps depending on the fractional part of the interpolated target. The D.14b Example repeats the error: 'floor(1000 - 32.4) = 967' is a shift of 33, and it then says 'moved 33 px'. The 'constant' claim is also false at 90 and 144 fps. f_q = floor(f) is taken from the interpolated target and changes every frame, while the Controller subtracts AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos_curr) + (0, -35), which steps once per tick (3 px at run). The aim can therefore differ by up to one tick's displacement, plus the independent-floor effect, even with a settled lag. There is no fixture dt in the AC.
findings.fix: Recompute from D.6/D.14b (G4). Rewrite the oracle as: 'with the cursor still and the avatar at a steady run, aim_point_shift = f_q - floor(pos_curr) is within 1 base px of -(lag_ss(dt) + tick_phase) and varies by no more than ceil(v/60) + 1 base px at 90 and 144 fps; exactly constant only at 60 fps with integer targets.' Give the dt explicitly and use lag_ss(dt) (30.9 at 60 fps, 31.8 at 144), as L1069 already does. In D.14b and Edge Cases L801, state the sawtooth bound, and state that the 32.4 px figure is the dt -> 0 upper bound, not the value that is drawn. Mirror the bound in Player Controller AC-PCI-056 and its Edge Case L797.

findings.section: Formulas D.14b Output Range (L644) / D.8b (L503) / C4 (L163) / OQ 18 - CLAMPED aim mismatch
findings.finding: Carried over; the previous pass did not land it. The GDD bounds the aim-vs-picture mismatch (pose_q - f_q) by L plus the inner-box correction, 'up to L_MAX_eff = 72' or '104 px' in C4 and OQ 18. D.8b states the limits clamp acts on the pose and 'the aim mapping's f_q is unaffected'. While the camera is CLAMPED, the picture centre c can sit far from f_q. D.8b's own example puts the avatar 170 px below picture centre while f_q = 960 and c = 820. A mouse player who places the cursor on a visible target near the hull edge gets cursor_world_aim = f_q + cursor_off, which is 140 px or more from the target. The beam then points away from, or even opposite to, where the cursor sits. That breaks the chest lamp, the game's main verb, whenever the camera is clamped. No AC covers it, and OQ 18's playtest item names only the lag + L case. The R4 ruling (f_q is canonical) is not reversed, but this consequence is not stated or bounded.
findings.fix: Keep R4's published f_q but make it limits-consistent. Publish f_q' = clamp(f_q, lo, hi), the same limits clamp applied to the follow term only, with no L, no inner-box and no jolt. That keeps the aim loop open, because the rect comes from the PROJECTOR, and it cuts the worst-case mismatch to at most L_MAX_eff. Update the D.14b Output Range and the registry mouse_to_world_aim entry. Add an AC: 'camera CLAMPED at hi_y, cursor on the avatar's sprite, aim direction points at the avatar to within AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX'. Player Controller conforms to the published value.

findings.section: Formulas D.6b (L445) vs D.8b (L503) vs D.9, registry follow_offset_quantised / limits_clamp
findings.finding: Carried over; not fixed. D.6b says pose_q = p + floor(o/Q)*Q 'the limits clamp (D.8b) is then applied to pose_q', and the registry follow_offset_quantised agrees ('then limits_clamp'). D.8b and the registry limits_clamp say the limits clamp comes first and 'then quantisation (D.9)' ('pose before quantisation'). D.6b is the default candidate. On that path an integer pose_q is clamped against lo/hi computed from the eased float rect_eff. For the transient after a detach or weld that moves the rect, the final pose is then non-integer, which breaks the whole-base-px camera rule and Pillar 1. No AC catches it: L1094 checks canvas scale only, and L1041 checks CanvasItem positions, not the canvas transform.
findings.fix: Pick one order and write it in one place. For the D.6b path use pose_q = floor(clamp(p + floor(o/Q)*Q, lo, hi) / Q) * Q, i.e. a re-floor after the limits clamp. Make D.8b, D.9 and both registry entries agree. Add an AC: 'during the 0.54 s rect ease the world canvas_transform origin is integral on every frame'.

findings.section: Formulas D.6b + AC L1069 + C3 ('one camera host computes p and hands it to the actor') vs PR-4 rule 2 and Player Controller Avatar Presenter
findings.finding: Carried over; not mirrored in any sibling. D.6b requires 'one camera host computes p once per frame and hands it to both the actor and the camera', and AC L1069 asserts the identity. PR-4 rule 2 and PR-8 item 5 say every presentation node computes its own floored position. The Player Controller GDD has no 'camera host' contract for its Avatar Presenter (grep of the Controller and Body returns nothing). findings.fix: Give the pipeline a published function, e.g. quantised_position(entity_id, tick_alpha) -> p, which the actor, the camera host and any other target all call. The invariant becomes 'same function, same frame, same inputs', which is testable without a hand-off. Add the function to Interactions row 3 and to Player Controller PC-14. The AC can then assert equality of calls rather than a handed-over value.

findings.section: Core Rules PR-4 rule 3 (L118), PR-11 table (L220), D.17 (L728), Game Feel (L958) - 'never twice in a frame' at real speeds
findings.finding: The G4 scoping fixed the frame-rate dimension but not the speed dimension. The unqualified wording 'camera and sprites step one base px ... never twice in a frame at f_render >= 60' is true only for a 1 px/tick body, which is what AC L1031 and PR-11 L223 correctly say. The shipped speeds are 2 px/tick (walk, 120 px/s) and 3 px/tick (run, 180 px/s). At 144 fps a run advances 1.25 px per frame, so p steps 1 or 2. At 90 fps a run steps exactly 2, and even a walk steps 1 or 2 (1.33 px/frame). Game Feel L958 ('at 144 and 90 fps ... never twice in a frame') is therefore false for run and for walk at 90 fps.
findings.fix: Replace 'never twice in a frame' in L118, L220, L728 and L958 with 'never more than ceil(v / f_render) base px in a frame, never backward' (1 px per frame holds for a 1 px/tick body at f_render >= 60, for walk at >= 120 fps, for run at >= 180 fps). AC L1033 is already scoped to walk at 144 fps and stays valid; add a run row to it.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria > Camera follow, look-ahead, cuts (mouse-aim AC, L1059) vs D.14b Example/Output Range (L644-645), Edge Cases L801, OQ 18
findings.finding: This is the same defect class as the three prior blockers: an (auto) AC whose oracle a correct implementation fails (G4). L1059 says that with a still cursor and a running avatar the aim is 'constant once the follow lag has settled' and shifted 'by exactly f_q - p, 32 px west of it ... 32 = floor(32.4)'. D.6 says lag is measured after the update. That lag is 30.9 px at 60 fps, 31.4 at 90 and 31.8 at 144, not lag_inf = 32.4. So f_q - p is 31 at 60 fps and 31 or 32 at 144 fps depending on the fractional part of the interpolated target. The D.14b Example repeats the error: 'floor(1000 - 32.4) = 967' is a shift of 33, and it then says 'moved 33 px'. The 'constant' claim is also false at 90 and 144 fps. f_q = floor(f) is taken from the interpolated target and changes every frame, while the Controller subtracts AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos_curr) + (0, -35), which steps once per tick (3 px at run). The aim can therefore differ by up to one tick's displacement, plus the independent-floor effect, even with a settled lag. There is no fixture dt in the AC.
findings.fix: Recompute from D.6/D.14b (G4). Rewrite the oracle as: 'with the cursor still and the avatar at a steady run, aim_point_shift = f_q - floor(pos_curr) is within 1 base px of -(lag_ss(dt) + tick_phase) and varies by no more than ceil(v/60) + 1 base px at 90 and 144 fps; exactly constant only at 60 fps with integer targets.' Give the dt explicitly and use lag_ss(dt) (30.9 at 60 fps, 31.8 at 144), as L1069 already does. In D.14b and Edge Cases L801, state the sawtooth bound, and state that the 32.4 px figure is the dt -> 0 upper bound, not the value that is drawn. Mirror the bound in Player Controller AC-PCI-056 and its Edge Case L797.

findings.section: Formulas D.14b Output Range (L644) / D.8b (L503) / C4 (L163) / OQ 18 - CLAMPED aim mismatch
findings.finding: Carried over; the previous pass did not land it. The GDD bounds the aim-vs-picture mismatch (pose_q - f_q) by L plus the inner-box correction, 'up to L_MAX_eff = 72' or '104 px' in C4 and OQ 18. D.8b states the limits clamp acts on the pose and 'the aim mapping's f_q is unaffected'. While the camera is CLAMPED, the picture centre c can sit far from f_q. D.8b's own example puts the avatar 170 px below picture centre while f_q = 960 and c = 820. A mouse player who places the cursor on a visible target near the hull edge gets cursor_world_aim = f_q + cursor_off, which is 140 px or more from the target. The beam then points away from, or even opposite to, where the cursor sits. That breaks the chest lamp, the game's main verb, whenever the camera is clamped. No AC covers it, and OQ 18's playtest item names only the lag + L case. The R4 ruling (f_q is canonical) is not reversed, but this consequence is not stated or bounded.
findings.fix: Keep R4's published f_q but make it limits-consistent. Publish f_q' = clamp(f_q, lo, hi), the same limits clamp applied to the follow term only, with no L, no inner-box and no jolt. That keeps the aim loop open, because the rect comes from the PROJECTOR, and it cuts the worst-case mismatch to at most L_MAX_eff. Update the D.14b Output Range and the registry mouse_to_world_aim entry. Add an AC: 'camera CLAMPED at hi_y, cursor on the avatar's sprite, aim direction points at the avatar to within AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX'. Player Controller conforms to the published value.

findings.section: Formulas D.6b (L445) vs D.8b (L503) vs D.9, registry follow_offset_quantised / limits_clamp
findings.finding: Carried over; not fixed. D.6b says pose_q = p + floor(o/Q)*Q 'the limits clamp (D.8b) is then applied to pose_q', and the registry follow_offset_quantised agrees ('then limits_clamp'). D.8b and the registry limits_clamp say the limits clamp comes first and 'then quantisation (D.9)' ('pose before quantisation'). D.6b is the default candidate. On that path an integer pose_q is clamped against lo/hi computed from the eased float rect_eff. For the transient after a detach or weld that moves the rect, the final pose is then non-integer, which breaks the whole-base-px camera rule and Pillar 1. No AC catches it: L1094 checks canvas scale only, and L1041 checks CanvasItem positions, not the canvas transform.
findings.fix: Pick one order and write it in one place. For the D.6b path use pose_q = floor(clamp(p + floor(o/Q)*Q, lo, hi) / Q) * Q, i.e. a re-floor after the limits clamp. Make D.8b, D.9 and both registry entries agree. Add an AC: 'during the 0.54 s rect ease the world canvas_transform origin is integral on every frame'.

findings.section: Core Rules PR-4 rule 3 (L118), PR-11 table (L220), D.17 (L728), Game Feel (L958) - 'never twice in a frame' at real speeds
